subsystems.name: Rotor
subsystems.role: a continuous loop of cable or mass stream moving faster than orbital velocity, whose outward centrifugal force supports the ring.

subsystems.name: Sheath
subsystems.role: the outer structure that contains the rotor and carries payloads; it moves slower or stays stationary.

subsystems.name: Magnetic suspension
subsystems.role: keeps the rotor centred without contact and transfers forces between rotor and sheath.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal control
subsystems.role: keeps the rotor spinning by compensating for losses, and rejects waste heat.

subsystems.name: Surface access
subsystems.role: tethers or elevators connect the ring to the ground or to floating platforms.

subsystems.name: Control and safety
subsystems.role: monitors structural dynamics, debris and station-keeping.

buildSteps.title: Develop off-Earth industry
buildSteps.detail: Mine asteroids or the Moon for metals and volatiles, and manufacture structural materials in orbit.

buildSteps.title: Build a seed ring
buildSteps.detail: Launch a small cable loop with a rotor into low Earth orbit to test magnetic levitation and dynamic support.

buildSteps.title: Spin up the rotor
buildSteps.detail: Use electromagnetic drives to accelerate the rotor to several kilometres per second, above orbital velocity, lifting the sheath.

buildSteps.title: Expand the ring
buildSteps.detail: Add segments to increase circumference and altitude, using materials produced by the seed ring itself.

buildSteps.title: Install power and control
buildSteps.detail: Attach solar arrays, radiators and computers to manage the ring's dynamics and energy losses.

buildSteps.title: Add surface access
buildSteps.detail: Deploy tethers from the ring to the surface or to high-altitude platforms for payload transport.

buildSteps.title: Commission and scale
buildSteps.detail: Test payload delivery, then expand to a full planetary ring.

prerequisites.why: lab-scale carbon nanotubes and graphene exist, but not in the kilometre-scale cables needed.
lunar samples and asteroid missions exist, but no industrial-scale extraction or refining.

prerequisites.tech: Magnetic levitation at high speed in vacuum
prerequisites.why: maglev trains operate at hundreds of km/h; scaling to km/s in vacuum is a leap but understood.
reusable rockets have cut costs, but not to the thousands of tonnes a ring would require.
no system today can track and avoid all debris for a structure spanning the planet.

pathway.milestone: reusable rockets and space stations enable routine access to low Earth orbit
lunar mining and orbital manufacturing produce structural materials off Earth
pathway.unlocks: materials for a seed ring without launching everything from the ground.

pathway.milestone: a low Earth orbit demonstrator ring supports its own weight and lifts a payload
pathway.unlocks: proof of dynamic support and magnetic suspension at scale.

pathway.milestone: a full planetary ring with surface access encircles Earth
pathway.unlocks: very low-cost launch to orbit and beyond.

pathway.milestone: rings around other planets or moons and interplanetary logistics
